flawed_step: The implication from equal adjacency spectra to graph isomorphism cannot be justified. The spectrum determines the common number of vertices and some graph invariants, but not the full adjacency relation.
counterexample: Let G be the star K_{1,4} on vertices {1,2,3,4,5}, with edges {12,13,14,15}. Let H be the disjoint union C_4 ⊔ K_1, with edges {12,23,34,41} and isolated vertex 5. The adjacency spectrum of K_{1,4} is {2,-2,0,0,0}. The spectrum of C_4 is {2,-2,0,0}, and adjoining an isolated vertex adds one zero eigenvalue, so H also has spectrum {2,-2,0,0,0}. Nevertheless, G and H are not isomorphic: G is connected and has degree sequence (4,1,1,1,1), whereas H is disconnected and has degree sequence (2,2,2,2,0).
assessment_summary: A proof attempt fails at the essential inference that cospectrality forces isomorphism. The explicit five-vertex graphs K_{1,4} and C_4 ⊔ K_1 are cospectral but nonisomorphic, so the statement is false.
